Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Nearly every outlet is leading with the dramatic reversal in U.S. stock markets, as a historic Democratic 'blue wave' in Tuesday's midterms first sparked a rally and then a brutal tech-led selloff over fears of tighter AI and data-center regulation. Coverage also converges on Anthropic's imminent blockbuster IPO and CVS Health's major corporate breakup, alongside a Bank of England rate hike and fallout from the U.S. election on business politics.

stories.headline: Tech-led selloff erases post-midterm stock rally as AI fears grip markets
stories.summary: The Nasdaq plunged into correction territory and the Dow dropped over 1,500 points as investors grew alarmed that Democratic midterm victories in states like Texas and Ohio signal a political backlash against the AI data-center buildout, with Axios calling it the worst showing since the April 2025 tariff panic.

stories.headline: CVS Health to split itself up, reversing $78 billion Aetna deal
stories.summary: CVS Health said it will split off its drugstore business, a move that would reverse its $78 billion Aetna acquisition and dismantle the vertically integrated healthcare conglomerate it built since 2018, with shares falling 10% on the news.

stories.headline: Anthropic's slowing growth and ballooning losses complicate record IPO math
stories.summary: Anthropic's third-quarter results showed slowing revenue growth and rising expenses, leading analysts to tell Fortune that institutional investors are pushing to price the IPO toward the lower end of its $1.5-2 trillion target range, with a valuation above $1.41 trillion implying a price-to-sales ratio achieved by just 14 of over 4,000 IPOs since 1980.

stories.headline: Bank of England raises interest rates for first time in three years
stories.summary: The Bank of England increased interest rates for the first time in more than three years and warned inflation would climb to about 5 percent next year, far above its target.

stories.headline: China blocks SoftBank's $5.4 billion robotics takeover
stories.summary: Chinese authorities stopped the sale of Swiss-owned ABB Robotics to Japan's SoftBank, a move that signals wider Beijing scrutiny of global transactions that could affect its technology ambitions.

stories.headline: Texas's business-friendly playbook rattled by Democratic sweep
stories.summary: NYT's DealBook examines how the Democrats' election sweep in Texas could rewrite the state's long-standing business-friendly policies, a shift closely watched given Texas's status as a major corporate and data-center hub.

stories.headline: Bangladesh raises minimum wage for garment workers after mass protests
stories.summary: Bangladesh agreed to raise the minimum wage for garment workers after hundreds of factories were shut down this week by protesting workers in the country, the world's second-largest clothing exporter.

stories.headline: Paraguay's president resigns as bank collapse tied to him sparks crisis
stories.summary: Santiago Peña's resignation followed the collapse of a bank with close ties to him, rattling a fast-growing South American economy that had attracted investors and forged close ties with the U.S.

Business.gaps: Puck had no business-relevant items found; WSJ, NYT, FT, The Economist, Politico, and BBC coverage was limited to feed items provided since these outlets block web search.

US politics.overview: Coverage overwhelmingly centers on the aftermath of Tuesday's midterm elections, which outlets across the spectrum describe as a historic 'blue wave' that gave Democrats control of both the House and Senate. Secondary threads include market jitters over the AI trade, the brewing leadership fights atop both parties, a wave of Trump-related legal news, and early state-level fallout from the election (California's death penalty, L.A.'s mayoral upset).

stories.headline: Democrats sweep Congress in historic 'blue wave'
stories.summary: Politico reports Republicans are absorbing what looks like a historic midterm defeat as Democrats retook both chambers of Congress, a result several outlets are calling a once-in-a-generation rout that reached deep into red territory.

stories.headline: Texas flips blue for the first time in three decades
stories.summary: Politico notes Republicans had run Texas for 30 years, but Democrats took the governorship, a Senate seat and other statewide offices on election night, a result Axios and RealClearPolitics both flagged as the night's single biggest shock.

stories.headline: Stocks tumble as post-election AI rally reverses
stories.summary: The New York Times reports the S&P 500 posted its worst daily decline in more than a year as the technology sector dragged markets down on worries about the durability of the AI buildout, even as WSJ detailed the Nasdaq's 5% plunge into correction territory.

stories.headline: Schumer and Thune both plan to stay atop their conferences despite opposite fortunes
stories.summary: Punchbowl News reports Chuck Schumer is riding high toward a second stint as majority leader after Democrats flipped the Senate, while John Thune is still expected to seek another term as GOP leader despite the scale of his party's losses, even as some senators blame him.

stories.headline: DOJ civil rights chief Harmeet Dhillon resigns after midterm blowout
stories.summary: NPR reports the head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division is stepping down after 18 tumultuous months, with Courthouse News noting her final act was deploying 1,000 DOJ election monitors nationwide for the first time in U.S. history.

stories.headline: Appeals court presses Trump on whether immunity shields his hush-money conviction
stories.summary: The Hill reports a New York appeals panel questioned Thursday whether presidential immunity or federal law bars Trump's criminal conviction over the 2016 hush-money payment, with Courthouse News quoting a justice pressing the defense on how the argument would benefit citizens.

stories.headline: GOP post-mortems point to Iran war and tariffs as the wave's true trigger
stories.summary: RealClearPolitics argues the GOP wipeout traces back to the Iran bombing campaign, a theme echoed by The Dispatch, which argues tariffs became the 'millstone' that sank Republicans and dismisses Vance's Iran-war theory as the sole culprit.

stories.headline: Newsom commutes all California death sentences to life without parole
stories.summary: The Hill reports Gov. Gavin Newsom is changing the penalty for all 548 death row inmates in the state, a move Courthouse News says Newsom called one of the hardest decisions of his career given its impact on victims' families.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS had no recent (last 48h) midterm or policy coverage available in search results; its most recent relevant item found was from April 2026, so it is omitted from the list above. Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian block web search, so only their provided feed items were used.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage overwhelmingly centers on the political and market fallout from this week's US midterms, where voters rejected data centers in nearly all ballot measures, triggering a historic AI stock selloff, a Texas gubernatorial upset, and scrambling PR responses from OpenAI and Meta. Secondary threads include new AI product launches (Anthropic's Personal Finance tool, Meta's Muse voice mode, OpenAI's cybersecurity model) and cross-border tech friction with China (chip export limits, a blocked robotics acquisition).

stories.headline: Nasdaq plunges as investors flee the AI trade after Democratic sweep
stories.summary: A broad tech-led selloff sent the Nasdaq into correction territory and the Dow down more than 1,500 points, as investors worried that a new Democratic Congress will curb the AI buildout; Bloomberg and NYT reported the S&P 500 posted its worst single-day decline in over a year, and SpaceX's default risk hit a record high in the same credit slump.

stories.headline: US voters overwhelmingly reject data centers at the ballot box
stories.summary: 404 Media reports that data center proposals were on the ballot in more than 40 races across 13 states and lost in at least 38 of them, while Texas Governor Greg Abbott — who branded the state the data center 'epicenter' — lost by over 700,000 votes to a Democrat who campaigned on a moratorium. The Register separately found nearly all examined gubernatorial candidates backed curbing data centers, and MIT Technology Review detailed how Texas's status as the AI buildout's hub is now in jeopardy.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Meta launch PR offensives to win back data-center communities
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced a 'National Community Compact' and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint with voluntary pledges to protect local resources, a move The Decoder notes came just two days after voters rejected new data centers in 40 of 41 ballot measures; Meta's president separately warned at the WSJ Tech conference that the backlash will make future AI expansion harder.

stories.headline: Anthropic lets Claude connect to your bank account with new Personal Finance tool
stories.summary: Anthropic announced that Claude users can now link bank and credit card accounts via Plaid to get read-only spending analysis, catching up to a similar ChatGPT feature; The Verge notes Anthropic says the tool cannot move or invest users' money.

stories.headline: Meta rolls out voice mode and expressive avatars for Muse AI
stories.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced that US users can now have real-time voice conversations with a customizable animated Muse avatar, part of a push ahead of a forthcoming wearable device built around the AI agent.

stories.headline: China blocks SoftBank's $5.4 billion robotics takeover
stories.summary: Chinese authorities stopped the sale of ABB Robotics, owned by a Swiss conglomerate, to Japan's SoftBank, reflecting wider Beijing scrutiny of global tech transactions that could affect its own technology ambitions.

stories.headline: 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips stuck in Hong Kong as Beijing withholds import approval
stories.summary: Reuters reported that roughly 600,000 of Nvidia's H200 chips are sitting in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China, with Beijing withholding approval for large-scale imports, underscoring ongoing US-China chip tensions.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model built to stay 'in scope'
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a model for finding exploitable vulnerabilities and developing fixes that it says avoided exploiting out-of-scope services over 99% of the time; TechCrunch questioned whether the release is sufficient given the industry's broader cybersecurity scrutiny, and The Register covered the model's 'rules of engagement' framing.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer, IEEE Spectrum, Rest of World, Wired, Ars Technica, and Google DeepMind had no new items directly on these top stories beyond what's cited; The Information's coverage was reflected only through its Nvidia/Apollo data-center story and broader data-center-economics pieces.

Energy.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections, which outlets like Latitude Media say is upending state-level energy and data-center policy, alongside the run-up to the COP31 climate summit opening in Antalya, Turkey. Trade and utility press are also tracking Trump administration moves on grid equipment and wind tariffs, while business outlets cover oil-market swings tied to geopolitics in the Middle East.

stories.headline: Democrats' midterm sweep set to rewire state energy and data-center policy
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that historic Democratic wins in Texas, Wisconsin, Ohio, Georgia, Michigan and Nevada governors' races and public utility commissions were driven largely by backlash to data centers and rising electricity bills, with several winners pledging moratoriums or new cost-sharing rules for data centers. In a companion piece, the outlet notes Georgia's PSC flipped to Democratic control for the first time in two decades and Michigan voters barred utilities from donating to state politicians.

stories.headline: Stocks surge, oil plummets after Democratic election victory
stories.summary: WSJ reports markets reacted sharply to the Democratic midterm victory, with equities rallying and oil prices falling, alongside news that CVS plans to break itself up.

stories.headline: COP31 opens in Antalya aiming for global electrification pledge
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports the COP31 summit, starting Nov. 9 in Antalya, Turkey, will push countries to commit to raising electricity's share of final energy demand to 35% by 2035 from about 20% today, though the goal remains voluntary. Carbon Brief is separately tracking the negotiating texts and a Brazil-led roadmap on fossil fuels and deforestation feeding into the talks.

stories.headline: Trump's ban on foreign-made grid components sparks industry pushback
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports stakeholders welcomed the order's grid-security goals but warned that restrictions based on country of origin rather than function threaten investment and practicality. Latitude Media separately notes the bulk power system order blocks equipment from 24 countries including China, which supplies roughly 65% of U.S. transformer equipment, and could raise prices once implementing rules appear in late December.

stories.headline: Revolution Wind offshore farm becomes fully operational despite Trump opposition
stories.summary: Canary Media reports the $6.2 billion Revolution Wind project is now running at full capacity, supplying power to three New England utilities despite repeated Trump administration efforts to halt it, while developer Ørsted also finished turbine foundations for the nearby Sunrise Wind project.

stories.headline: Iran escalates guerrilla tactics to disrupt Strait of Hormuz oil flows
stories.summary: WSJ reports Tehran is using tactics ranging from rocket-propelled grenades to limpet mines in an attempt to disrupt oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Toyota's hybrid sales surge as gas prices rise and EV demand slows
stories.summary: NYT reports Toyota's stock jumped as high U.S. gas prices boosted hybrid sales, though shifting political winds in Washington could threaten the company's advantage.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco's profits hold up despite wartime damage to facilities
stories.summary: The Economist, covering majority state-owned Saudi Aramco, reports that higher oil prices have more than offset the impact of attacks on the company's facilities, keeping profits strong.

Energy.gaps: Heatmap News: search returned only older archival articles (mostly from the past year), nothing identifiable from the last 48 hours. E&E News: its energy/environment coverage has moved to Politico Pro, and available search results were months old with nothing fresh found. Argus Media: no feed items were provided and a dedicated search could not be run within the query limit, so no current coverage could be confirmed.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by Hong Kong's 10-year sentencing of democracy activist Joshua Wong and Beijing's decision to block SoftBank's $5.4bn purchase of ABB's robotics unit, both drawing international pushback. Business and tech outlets are tracking Beijing's efforts to stabilize a wobbling stock market, fresh US tech-supply-chain pressure on Chinese firms, and fallout from the US midterms for US-China relations.

stories.headline: Hong Kong sentences Joshua Wong to 10 more years for foreign collusion
stories.summary: Hong Kong's national security police welcomed a 10-year prison term handed to jailed pro-democracy leader Joshua Wong after he pleaded guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces, his second conviction under the Beijing-imposed security law, as rights groups and international governments condemned the ruling.

stories.headline: China blocks SoftBank's $5.4bn takeover of ABB's robotics unit
stories.summary: Chinese regulators have stopped the sale of Swiss-owned ABB's robotics division to Japan's SoftBank, a deal valued at roughly $5.4 billion that Masayoshi Son had framed as a major push into AI-driven robotics, with Nikkei Asia noting that China has simply balked at the plan amid broader scrutiny of cross-border tech deals.

stories.headline: Oracle reportedly cancels $7 billion Tencent AI chip lease under US pressure
stories.summary: Oracle has scrapped a five-year, roughly $7 billion deal to lease advanced AI chips to Tencent after pressure from the Trump administration, underscoring tightening US controls on Chinese access to high-end computing power.

stories.headline: PBOC pledges more support to stabilize sliding Chinese stock market
stories.summary: People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng outlined plans to broaden long-term investment channels and bolster state investor Central Huijin's role as a market stabilizer after a string of declines in mainland stocks, following earlier swap-facility and relending measures this week.

stories.headline: Democrats' midterm sweep seen as both opportunity and challenge for China ties
stories.summary: Analysts say the Democrats' sweeping midterm win giving them control of Congress presents China with both openings and new complications in managing the US relationship, a theme also explored by Taipei Times and Caixin commentary on what a divided Washington means for trade and tech policy toward Beijing.

stories.headline: Rare strike at Taiwan chip plant exposes labor unrest in the AI boom
stories.summary: Workers at a Micron facility in Taoyuan staged a protest demanding a greater share of profits and better bonuses, highlighting friction between frontline manufacturing staff and the windfalls flowing to AI-driven chipmakers.

stories.headline: China dismisses accusations it is 'squeezing out' other economies
stories.summary: China's vice premier brushed off what he called "completely unfounded" concerns that Beijing was crowding out other economies as he opened a major import-focused business fair aimed at courting foreign buyers.

stories.headline: A loyal journalist takes the helm of China's state press association
stories.summary: China Media Project profiles Cui Shixin, newly appointed to run the All-China Journalists Association, describing him as an ideal fit for an organization that is state-run in all but name and puts Communist Party interests above press professionalism.

China.gaps: Global Times, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, and Yicai Global did not surface distinct recent China-politics/economy stories in search results beyond items already reflected via other outlets; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, WSJ and The Economist were only checked via the provided feed items since they block web search.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Israeli outlets is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's US midterm elections and what it means for the ongoing Iran war, Gulf-US security ties, and Israel's political deadlock, alongside a fresh wave of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Business desks are tracking Saudi Aramco's war-era profits, Emaar's $3.3 billion buyout, and the economic toll of the regional conflict on Gulf states.

stories.headline: Iran reports new wave of tanker attacks in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards and army said five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, with Tehran continuing to restrict traffic through a waterway that normally carries about a fifth of global oil consumption. The US military has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and has been helping tankers transit the strait.

stories.headline: Herzog says Eisenkot won majority of recommendations but delays mandate to Sunday
stories.summary: President Isaac Herzog said factions totaling 67 lawmakers recommended Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to form Israel's next government versus 46 for Netanyahu, but said he would hold further talks before formally handing over the mandate on Sunday given mutual vetoes between blocs. Separately, Avigdor Liberman was reported open to sitting with Haredi parties, a reversal of long-held policy.

stories.headline: US midterm wipeout complicates Gulf security ties and Israel aid
stories.summary: WSJ reports that billions of dollars in outstanding military orders are complicating efforts to wind down US aid to Israel as Democratic midterm gains bring greater scrutiny of the assistance, part of a broader shakeup following Trump's setback over the Iran war. AGBI's analysis similarly argued the Iran war could escalate before it de-escalates following the Republican defeat, with the region's reliance on Washington becoming a political liability.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco keeps posting strong profits despite war damage
stories.summary: The Economist reports that higher oil prices have more than offset the cost of bombed facilities, allowing Saudi Aramco to keep generating large profits even as the kingdom remains under attack. AGBI separately noted Aramco cut capital expenditure even as revenue and profit rose, while betting on fresh demand as the world rebuilds oil stockpiles.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia faces tough choices on Houthi threat after $51 billion peace demand
stories.summary: The WSJ reports that Riyadh asked Iran-backed Houthi militants what it would take to achieve peace, and received a demand for $51 billion, leaving the kingdom with no easy options as it weighs how to respond to the escalating threat.

stories.headline: Emaar board approves $3.3 billion buyout to delist construction unit
stories.summary: Emaar's board approved a plan to take its construction unit private in a $3.3 billion buyout and delist it from the Dubai exchange. AGBI separately reported the move as part of Emaar's plan for a full takeover of the Dubai-listed property unit.

stories.headline: UAE companies brace for new nine-hour daily driving limit
stories.summary: Analysts told The National that new UAE rules capping commercial drivers to nine hours behind the wheel per day will improve road safety but cause significant operational upheaval for logistics and transport companies.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes and gunfire kill five in Gaza as raids hit southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed five people in Gaza on Thursday, including a 12-year-old boy, according to rescue services cited by AFP, while separate Israeli air strikes targeted towns in Lebanon's Nabatieh and Tyre districts.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Gulf News, Khaleej Times, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al-Monitor-equivalent for Iran International, Ynetnews and Haaretz yielded no distinct recent lead stories beyond routine consumer/lifestyle items (e.g. Khaleej Times fuel price updates); Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and BBC block search so only feed items were used for those where provided.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage is dominated by a wave of high-stakes court rulings across the continent - in Tanzania, Somalia and Nigeria - that are reshaping opposition politics, alongside South Africa's tense municipal elections. Business and economy coverage centers on a mining crackdown in Congo, a diplomatic row over gold miners between Guinea and Burkina Faso, and fintech/banking stories from Kenya and Nigeria.

stories.headline: South Africa's municipal elections set up messy coalition talks
stories.summary: African Business reports that South Africa's municipal elections are unlikely to produce strong majorities in many regions, setting up tough coalition negotiations; Africa Confidential separately flagged how uncertainty over Jacob Zuma's health is complicating the MK Party's electoral calculus ahead of the vote.

stories.headline: Tundu Lissu treason verdict looms over Tanzania's judiciary
stories.summary: With three judges set to rule on opposition leader Tundu Lissu's fate, The Africa Report says the treason case's disputed evidence and prolonged detention have already raised serious doubts about judicial independence in Tanzania; Africa Confidential frames the verdict as a test of President Samia's political record.

stories.headline: Somalia's top court strikes down Mohamud's term extension
stories.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court has ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's one-year extension of his term was unlawful, a decision that follows violent clashes between government forces and the opposition over the move.

stories.headline: Nigerian court throws out Atiku Abubakar's presidential bid
stories.summary: A Nigerian court has nullified Atiku Abubakar's nomination as the African Democratic Congress's presidential candidate, upending the opposition's plans just two months before the election.

stories.headline: DR Congo orders probe after seizing illegal copper and cobalt shipments
stories.summary: Congolese officials seized thousands of tons of copper and cobalt, prompting the justice minister to order an investigation into widespread illegal mining, according to Mining Weekly's Bloomberg-sourced report.

stories.headline: Access Bank chair: Africa needs integration before a common currency
stories.summary: Access Bank Group chairman Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede argues African financial institutions should prioritize productive finance and deeper economic integration over pursuing a continental currency.

stories.headline: Safaricom's M-PESA overdraft service sees surging revenue
stories.summary: Safaricom generated roughly $38 million from its M-PESA Fuliza overdraft product as the number of borrowers using the service to complete transactions continues to climb.

Africa.gaps: The Continent could not be confirmed via search beyond generic archive/homepage listings, so no current story could be verified. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block search and had no relevant Africa items in the provided feed, so they could not be assessed for this period.

Media.overview: Media coverage over the past 48 hours is dominated by the fallout from the US midterms—ratings wars among cable networks, MAGA media infighting, and a DOJ leak probe tied to Politico—alongside structural industry stories: Meta's publisher-content fight, The New York Times' subscriber milestone and looming AI lawsuit windfall, Salon's shutdown, and Disney's upcoming layoffs.

stories.headline: NYT Adds 420,000 Digital Subscribers, Stays on Pace for 15 Million Goal
stories.summary: The New York Times added 420,000 new digital subscribers in Q3 2026, keeping it on pace to hit its goal of 15 million subscriptions by the end of 2027, with its CEO crediting 'human made journalism' for the growth.

stories.headline: Publishers Say Meta Is Holding Them 'Hostage' Over New AI Scraping Terms
stories.summary: Publisher trade groups worldwide are pushing back against Meta's new terms of service that could let it scrape content for AI without compensation, but heads of audience told Digiday they still can't afford to quit Facebook because of its reach for subscriptions and engagement.

stories.headline: Salon Shuts Down After 31 Years
stories.summary: The pioneering digital news site Salon announced it is closing after three decades, with site leadership calling it hard to find the right words for the end of something that meant so much to so many people.

stories.headline: DOJ Escalates Criminal Probe Into Supreme Court's Politico Leak
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors have issued grand jury subpoenas as they renew a criminal investigation into the 2022 leak of the Supreme Court's draft opinion overturning Roe v. Wade, which was first published by Politico.

stories.headline: What Could the Times Buy With an OpenAI Settlement?
stories.summary: Puck reports that OpenAI and Microsoft are widely expected to settle The New York Times' copyright lawsuit, potentially yielding up to a billion dollars that could fund another M&A spree for the paper after reply briefs are due November 20.

stories.headline: MAGA Media Turns on Itself After Midterm Losses
stories.summary: Status reports that after Democrats' election-night victory, MAGA media figures are turning on one another over the GOP's losses and telling Status the party must move on from Trump.

stories.headline: Disney Expected to Lay Off Thousands in Biggest Cuts of the Year
stories.summary: Disney is preparing its fourth and largest round of 2026 layoffs, with managers told to cut annualized expenses by 20% as CEO Josh D'Amaro looks to reinvest savings into film, TV, tech and theme parks.

stories.headline: UK Government Names 50 Local News Publishers Sharing £6m Grant
stories.summary: The UK government distributed £6 million in funding to 50 local publishers and seven industry projects, part of continued efforts to shore up struggling local journalism.

Media.gaps: No recent media-industry coverage found from NYT, WSJ, FT, The Guardian, Poynter (beyond midterms commentary), Adweek, Mediaite, or CJR beyond what's listed above since those outlets block search or their feed items skewed toward politics/election coverage rather than media-industry news.
